ideas.ablation_behavior_off: Set t_beh to the baseline empirical occupancy target independent of transition weights (or w_i=1 and t from item-uniform mass), while retaining Lorentz distances, soft occupancy, and loss weight.
ideas.ablation_both_on: Use train-only transition-mass targets and Lorentzian soft code assignments/prefix occupancy; export ordinary hard RQ SIDs and evaluate the locked Stage3 protocol.
ideas.ablation_geometry_off: Replace exp_o and d_L by matched-dimensional Euclidean squared distances in assignment probabilities; retain identical transition-derived targets, τ, objective and parameter budget.
ideas.behavior_computation: On train.parquet only, form within-user chronological adjacent pairs i→j. Set q_i=log(1+outdegree_i) and edge weight a_ij=count(i→j)/(sqrt(1+train_item_frequency(j))); define w_i=1+q_i and prefix target t_p^l proportional to Σ_i w_i·Σ_j a_ij for items i assigned under the current prefix p, with targets updated only from training-derived counts and frozen baseline prefix assignments (recommended to avoid target drift). Normalize targets separately per level.
ideas.behavior_signal: Training-only outgoing continuation mass per source item and per resulting SID prefix.
ideas.cost_estimate: One training adjacency pass O(E_train), sparse prefix-target tables, plus soft assignment already comparable to baseline. At frozen full-item scale 24,556×24×3,000=1,768,032,000 item-stage evaluations; the added operation is O(BLK) for minibatch B, L levels, K codes, plus O(number of observed prefixes) target aggregation. Expect about 5–15% tokenizer wall-clock overhead with sparse prefix accumulation; Stage3 unchanged.
ideas.coupling_equation: p_i^l(k)=softmax_k[-d_L(exp_o(r_i^l),exp_o(c_k^l))²/τ]; m_p^l=Σ_i w_i Π_{s≤l}p_i^s(p_s); L_occ=Σ_l KL(t_beh^l || m_Lorentz^l). The behavior target t_beh and curved-distance-generated occupancy m_Lorentz meet in the same differentiable objective.
ideas.coupling_path: Train transition mass defines the target distribution over prefixes; Lorentzian distances define soft code memberships and their multi-level prefix occupancy; the KL gradient moves code parameters until geometry-induced memberships better match behavior mass.
ideas.falsifiable_hypothesis: Training continuation mass has useful hierarchical structure that static content loss underrepresents; both-on should shift codebook gradients and prefix populations toward predictive continuation regions and improve validation-selected Stage3 test Recall@10, with target >0.065. Verify changed prefix occupancies and parameter updates, not just SID quality.
ideas.hyperbolic_location: The soft code assignment probabilities used to compute differentiable subtree occupancies, and thus the prefix-mass training gradient in Stage2 RQ-VAE.
ideas.hyperbolic_operator: Lorentz-hyperboloid geodesic distance d_L at fixed curvature -κ, κ>0; use Lorentz exponential map at the origin for residual and code points.
ideas.key_change: At each RQ level, derive a fixed continuation-mass target for each partial SID prefix from training transitions, and train prefix prototypes so their Lorentzian soft occupancy matches that distribution. The occupancy gradient changes the codebook parameters that determine the discrete prefixes.
ideas.leakage_boundary: All edge counts, item frequencies, source weights, and baseline assignments are constructed from training rows only; validation/test interactions are not used in target formation, SID fitting, or cache updates. Evaluate held-out Stage3 splits only after the tokenizer and SIDs are frozen.
ideas.motivation: Flat item reconstruction allocates RQ capacity without regard to how much next-item probability a prefix needs to distinguish; popular continuation regions can consume disproportionate prediction mass.
ideas.novelty: This does not add successor geometry to each item's code score or steer residuals. It uses training-only continuation probability mass as a differentiable target for the occupancy of *entire code-prefix subtrees*, and matches that mass using Lorentzian subtree prototypes.
ideas.observables: Nonzero, finite gradients to codebooks/encoder; changed per-level hard prefixes relative to baseline; closer training-only prefix mass calibration; and, decisively, matched Stage3 test Recall@10. Compare all three required arms under identical selection and seeds.
risks: Mass matching may merely encode popularity, overwhelm reconstruction, or create a few overloaded prefixes; soft products can vanish at deep levels; target counts may be sparse. Tune a small loss-weight grid on validation and report popularity-stratified recall.
ideas.safeguards: Compute Lorentz vectors in float32/64; project to future hyperboloid after updates; clamp acosh argument to ≥1+ε and exp-map tangent norms; use log-domain products or clamp p≥ε at deeper levels; normalize t/m with epsilon and smooth rare prefixes; cap w_i and λ; monitor gradient norms, occupancy entropy and reconstruction; deterministic tie-breaking. Keep target table frozen to baseline assignments to prevent feedback loops.
ideas.spec_equations: For hyperboloid signature (-,+,...), <X,Y>_L=-X0Y0+Σ_{d>0}XdYd; d_L(X,Y)=acosh(max(1,-κ<X,Y>_L))/sqrt(κ). For each level l, x_i^l=exp_o(r_i^l), q_k^l=exp_o(c_k^l), p_i^l=softmax(-d_L(x_i^l,q_k^l)^2/τ). For prefix p=(k1,...,kl), m_p^l=ε+Σ_i w_i∏_{s=1}^l p_i^s(ks), normalize m over p. Freeze t_p^l from train-only baseline hard SID assignments and transition masses; L=L_base+λΣ_l KL(t^l||m^l). Stop gradient through t. Use straight-through hard argmin for normal RQ forward/export; soft occupancy is a training auxiliary directly shaping the same code vectors.
ideas.spec_inputs_outputs: Inputs: training sequences, frozen baseline SIDs for target aggregation, train item frequencies, current residuals and codebooks, κ, τ, λ. Outputs: frozen per-level prefix target tables, differentiable occupancy loss and gradients, then hard per-item RQ digits/SIDs.

specification.text: Build assignments p_i^l(k) with a temperature-softmax of negative Lorentz distances from current residual points to level-l code points; define soft prefix mass m_p^l as the sum over items of w_i times the product of their assignments along prefix p. Set w_i to a smoothed training continuation mass (defined below), normalize w to mean one, and minimize L_occ=Σ_l KL(stopgrad(t^l)||m^l), where t_p^l is the normalized training-only probability mass of transitions whose source item has prefix p. Compute m with differentiable products and normalize with epsilon. Keep baseline reconstruction and commitment losses; hard SID export remains ordinary argmin RQ.

ideas.title: Fit hierarchical code occupancy to training continuation mass in Lorentz space

ideas.ablation_behavior_off: Shuffle cohort labels within each target while preserving class counts and all geometry/loss settings; this destroys user-behavior correspondence while retaining the same pair budget.
ideas.ablation_both_on: Train with the unshuffled train-only cohort labels and Lorentz geodesic margin, alongside baseline RQ-VAE losses; export hard SIDs and run the same Stage3 evaluation.
ideas.ablation_geometry_off: Replace Lorentz exp/distance by Euclidean representation and Euclidean norm in the same pair margin, keeping labels, dimensions, pair samples and margin calibration matched.
ideas.behavior_computation: Using only train sequences, enumerate (user, source i, target j) adjacent transitions; context is mean Stage1 vector of preceding up-to-five distinct training items. For each target j with ≥20 transitions, run deterministic k-means (K=min(4, floor(n_j/5))) on context vectors and label each transition; pair distinct source items with the same target and different cohort labels as positives, same cohort as negatives. Exclude users/targets below support threshold.
ideas.behavior_signal: Cross-user context cohort identity for transitions into a shared next item.
ideas.cost_estimate: One train transition/context preprocessing pass O(E_train·d), cohort clustering on sampled contexts, then O(Pd) Lorentz pair distances per step for P sampled pairs. At frozen scale 24,556 items ×24 steps/epoch ×3,000 epochs, cache transition pairs and draw e.g. P=2B per minibatch; expect 5–20% overhead depending on pair count/dimension, no Stage3 inference cost.
ideas.coupling_equation: L_pair(a,b)=1[y_diff]·max(0,m-d_L(exp_o(q_a),exp_o(q_b)))² + 1[y_same]·max(0,d_L(exp_o(q_a),exp_o(q_b))-M)², where y_diff comes only from training-user context cohort labels.
ideas.coupling_path: Training user-context cohorts determine positive/negative pair labels; those labels select the margin branch applied to Lorentz distance between the exact quantized representations underlying the SIDs, changing their codebook/encoder updates.
ideas.falsifiable_hypothesis: For targets with multiple user-context cohorts, the cohort distinction is predictive rather than noise; preserving it in curved code representations will change relevant SID digits and improve validation-selected Stage3 test Recall@10 toward/above 0.065. Confirm that pairwise distance margins and held-out-within-train cohort-conditioned next-item diagnostics change alongside test recall.
ideas.hyperbolic_location: A contrastive margin loss on the level-l quantized item points; gradients pass through Lorentz distance to the encoder/codebook that produces the SID digits.
ideas.hyperbolic_operator: Lorentz geodesic distance on curvature -κ, κ>0, between origin-exp-mapped quantized source representations.
ideas.key_change: Sample pairs of training examples with the same next item but different preceding user-context cohorts; encourage the source-item SID representations to preserve the observed cohort contrast at each RQ level via a Lorentzian geodesic margin. The contrast term acts on the actual residual/code representation used to construct SIDs.
ideas.leakage_boundary: Build contexts, target groupings, cohort centroids/labels and pairs strictly from train rows and training-period histories; freeze them before Stage2 fitting. Do not use validation/test targets, user histories, labels or interaction statistics for pairs or SID assignment.
ideas.motivation: A target item can follow similar textual items for one user cohort and a different set for another; ordinary itemwise quantization can erase these user-conditioned distinctions even when next-item prediction needs them.
ideas.novelty: Rather than a per-item branch vector or successor barycenter, this uses pairwise contrastive comparisons between same-target transitions from different users, with the contrast margin defined by hyperbolic distance between quantized source representations. It is a relational training signal, not a behavior term appended to Euclidean nearest-code assignment.
ideas.observables: Pair margins become satisfied without reconstruction collapse; cohort-conditioned hard SID distances/assignments change; Stage3 test Recall@10 improves versus both toggles. Report performance by target support and cohort multiplicity.
risks: Same-target cohort labels may reflect sampling noise, item popularity, or history length; the pair loss can conflict with semantic reconstruction or over-separate paraphrastic items. Sparse targets yield few reliable pairs; cohort clustering can be unstable.
ideas.safeguards: Require target support and multiple cohorts; cap pairs per target/user to avoid popularity domination; L2-normalize context vectors before clustering; fix clustering seed and label ordering; compute Lorentz distance in float32/64 with acosh clamp and hyperboloid projection; clip gradients; use zero pair loss for invalid/rare items; monitor reconstruction and pair-label balance. Set m<M with margins selected on training-only distance quantiles and λ via validation protocol.
ideas.spec_equations: Let q_i^l be the straight-through quantized tangent representation at level l; map X_i=exp_o^{(-κ)}(q_i^l) to the Lorentz sheet. d(X,Y)=acosh(max(1,-κ<X,Y>_L))/sqrt(κ). Given pair label y=1 for different cohorts, L_pair=y[m-d]_+² +(1-y)[d-M]_+². Total objective L_base+λ L_pair; sample balanced pairs and average. Hard SID indices remain standard nearest-code indices, but the pair gradient updates the same encoder/codebook points and therefore can alter assignments on subsequent steps.
ideas.spec_inputs_outputs: Inputs: train-only transitions and contexts, frozen Stage1 item embeddings, deterministic per-target cohort labels/pair sampler, RQ-VAE level representations/codebooks, κ,m,M,λ. Outputs: pair loss/gradients and updated code parameters; ordinary hard SID digits.

specification.text: From each train transition (u,i→j), form context vector h_u,i as the mean of frozen Stage1 embeddings of up to the previous 5 train items, excluding j. For same target j, pair contexts from different users; define y_ab=1 if their contexts fall in different deterministic training-only k-means cohorts, else 0. Let z_ab be their source-item quantized Lorentz points at a selected level; optimize L_pair= y·max(0,m-d_L(z_a,z_b))² +(1-y)·max(0,d_L(z_a,z_b)-M)² with 0<m<M, sampled balanced pairs. To avoid pulling identical source item copies apart inconsistently, pair only distinct source items; use the item's code representation as z.

ideas.title: Preserve cross-user successor contrasts with a Lorentzian pairwise code margin

ideas.ablation_behavior_off: Replace h_i by the training-item population mean (equivalently remove item-specific branch calibration), preserving the same hyperbolic distance and parameterization.
ideas.ablation_both_on: Use training-only h_i, exp map, fixed-curvature Poincare distance and radial shell penalty in every residual code assignment as specified.
ideas.ablation_geometry_off: Keep the same training-derived h_i and radius penalty, but replace Poincare distances/maps/radii with Euclidean distance and Euclidean norm using matched scale.
ideas.behavior_computation: From the training split only, count consecutive item pairs (i,j) within each user's chronologically ordered training history, obtain smoothed p(j|i), then compute normalized outgoing entropy h_i. Do not use validation/test sequences or their item transitions.
ideas.cost_estimate: One train-only transition count pass O(number of training transitions), plus O(N*K*D) distance work per quantization stage, same asymptotic assignment cost as baseline and typically a modest constant-factor increase for Poincare distances and one scalar penalty. At frozen scale N=24,556, 24 steps/epoch, 3,000 epochs: 73,668,000 item-stage opportunities per stage over training; the extra radius/penalty is O(1) per item-codeword comparison, while distance computation is the dominant added work. Cache h_i and rho_i; no user graph is traversed during epochs.
ideas.coupling_equation: k_i^s = argmin_k [ d_c(x_i^s,c_sk)^2 + lambda_r*(d_c(0,c_sk)-rho_i/S)^2 ], where rho_i=rho_min+(rho_max-rho_min)*h_i and d_c is the negatively curved Poincare distance.
ideas.coupling_path: Training transitions -> h_i -> rho_i -> shell-calibrated Poincare codeword argmin -> selected residual codeword and SID; setting h_i constant removes item-specific shell calibration, while replacing d_c with Euclidean distance removes curved assignment geometry.
ideas.falsifiable_hypothesis: Continuation branching varies meaningfully across items and is reflected in useful semantic hierarchy: higher-branching items should occupy broader/deeper code regions and yield more predictable generative prefixes, ultimately improving Stage3 test Recall@10, with a keep criterion of Recall@10 > 0.065 and a gain over both ablations.
ideas.hyperbolic_location: The residual quantizer's codeword assignment and straight-through quantization objective at every RQ stage.
ideas.hyperbolic_operator: Squared Poincare-ball distance d_c^2 at fixed negative curvature -c, plus geodesic distance from origin d_c(0,c_sk) as a radial shell measure; exp^c_0 maps encoder vectors into the ball.
ideas.key_change: Estimate item continuation branching from training sequences, map its normalized entropy to a desired hyperbolic radius, and jointly assign each item to the residual codeword minimizing a radius-calibrated Poincare distance. The resulting selected codeword is the RQ-VAE SID token and the assignment distance supplies the quantization gradient.
ideas.leakage_boundary: Freeze the training-derived h_i lookup before RQ-VAE SID export. Validation and test interactions are excluded from counts, smoothing support, entropy, shell targets, codebook assignments, and any SID-generation input; validation may only be used for model selection under the existing protocol.
ideas.motivation: Items that occur after sharply different user-interest branches need semantic codes that preserve those distinct continuation roles, while generic item similarity can collapse them.
ideas.novelty: Rather than append a graph feature, smooth embeddings, or add a separate hyperbolic loss, this changes the actual residual-code assignment metric: a train-only continuation-branch statistic determines each item's radial target in a negatively curved space.
ideas.observables: SID code assignments should shift systematically with h_i and codeword geodesic radii; quantizer gradients/codebook updates should change; measure prefix next-item accuracy and Stage3 test Recall@10, targeting >0.065. Report code utilization and reconstruction only as diagnostics, not admission criteria.
risks: The static item-level branch entropy may conflate genuine multi-interest branching with sparse/noisy observations; radial pressure may distort reconstruction or cause codebook underuse. Fixed curvature and shell scale require tuning on training-only diagnostics/validation protocol without using validation interactions to construct SIDs.
ideas.safeguards: Clamp encoder/map inputs inside radius (1-epsilon)/sqrt(c); use stable log1p/atanh distance evaluation and epsilon denominators; clamp computed distances and h_i to finite ranges. Use a minimum successor count or smoothing, explicitly set under-supported items to h_i=0, normalize by log support only for support >=2, initialize codewords inside the ball, and monitor NaN/overflow and code occupancy. Detach h_i/rho_i from gradients.
ideas.spec_equations: Counts n_ij from training-only consecutive pairs; p(j|i)=(n_ij+alpha)/(sum_l n_il+alpha*|N_i|) over observed successor support N_i; h_i=H(p_i)/log(max(2,|N_i|)) (set h_i=0 when |N_i|<2); rho_i=rho_min+(rho_max-rho_min)h_i. x_i=exp^c_0(z_i). At stage s, select k*=argmin_k d_c(x_i^s,c_sk)^2+lambda_r[d_c(0,c_sk)-rho_i/S]^2; q_i^s=c_sk*; update residual with the baseline RQ-VAE rule and optimize its reconstruction/commitment losses using straight-through gradients. Constants alpha, c, lambda_r, rho bounds are fixed before comparison and identical across behavior ablations where applicable.
ideas.spec_inputs_outputs: Inputs are training-only user-ordered item sequences, encoder outputs, residual codebooks, fixed c and shell hyperparameters. Outputs are cached h_i/rho_i, selected residual code indices at each stage, and the resulting SID sequence.

specification.text: For training sequences only, estimate smoothed next-item distributions p(j|i) from consecutive items; define h_i=H(p(.|i))/log(max(2, number_of_observed_successors_i)), with h_i=0 for no observed successors. Let z_i be the current Euclidean encoder output, map to ball x_i=exp^c_0(z_i), and set target radius rho_i=rho_min+(rho_max-rho_min)h_i. For each residual stage s and residual point x_i^s, project x_i^s to the ball, compute d_c(x_i^s,c_sk)^2 + lambda_r*(d_c(0,c_sk)-rho_i/S)^2 for each codeword k, choose argmin k, subtract the selected codeword via the existing residual update, and train with straight-through quantization plus commitment loss. Use shared fixed c>0; rho_i/S expresses a per-stage shell target, not a claim that residual radii add exactly.

ideas.title: User-branching-calibrated hyperbolic code shells

ideas.ablation_behavior_off: Set h_i=0 and hence v_i=0 while retaining identical curved quantization and all other settings.
ideas.ablation_both_on: Use training-derived h_i and the curvature -0.5 Poincare displacement and assignment as specified.
ideas.ablation_geometry_off: Replace exp/log/d_c with identity maps and squared Euclidean distance, preserving h_i and the behavior-dependent displacement formula in Euclidean space.
ideas.behavior_computation: From training-only user sequences in timestamp order, count adjacent item pairs (i,j); discard self-loops, retain top 16 outgoing successors by count, apply count^0.75 normalization, and average corresponding frozen item embeddings to form h_i.
ideas.behavior_signal: Directed next-item transition distribution, preserving branching rather than reducing each item to one neighbor.
ideas.cost_estimate: Precompute sparse transition summaries once; per epoch batch cost is O(B*16*d + B*L*K*d) with the extra O(B*d) map operations; codebook comparison already dominates. At frozen scale (24,556 items, 24 steps/epoch, 3,000 epochs), this adds 24*3,000*B*16*d arithmetic for context aggregation (or cache h_i and pay O(24,556*16*d) once), plus O(24*3,000*B*L*d) curved maps; no extra model passes. Expect roughly 5-15% step time depending on batch and codebook sizes.
ideas.coupling_path: Training transition counts make h_i; h_i determines b_i; the curved log map from z_i to b_i determines y_i; y_i changes the distances and chosen residual code at every level.
ideas.falsifiable_hypothesis: Items with branching successor distributions need a context-aware residual direction; the coupled assignment should improve Stage3 test Recall@10, targeting >0.065, and make leading SID prefixes more predictive of the training successor distribution. Keep only if both-on beats baseline and both ablations.
ideas.hyperbolic_location: The behavior-conditioned displacement is formed in the Poincare tangent space before each RQ-VAE residual quantizer assignment.
ideas.hyperbolic_operator: Poincare-ball exp^c and log^c maps plus geodesic distance, fixed sectional curvature -0.5.
ideas.key_change: Build a sparse distribution over next-item contexts for each item from training sequences, map its context centroid to the Poincare ball, and use that point to define a context-dependent tangent displacement before every residual quantizer assignment.
ideas.leakage_boundary: Construct all counts from the training interaction split only, freeze h_i before RQ-VAE fitting, and never read validation/test sequences when creating transition statistics or SIDs.
ideas.motivation: A single item embedding may participate in distinct next-item contexts; ordinary residual quantization can average those contexts and obscure which continuation a prefix implies.
ideas.novelty: Unlike a graph-denoised residual or behavior-only SID suffix, this changes the actual residual codebook assignment metric by transporting a train-only, context-conditioned direction through a negatively curved latent space.
ideas.observables: Changed code assignments and encoder/codebook gradients for branching items; compare successor-distribution predictability from SID prefixes and Stage3 test Recall@10.
risks: Sparse or noisy transitions may overfit; frequent successors may dominate; curvature/maps can destabilize mixed precision; the context adjustment may hurt semantic reconstruction and create worse prefixes.
ideas.safeguards: Clip tangent norms to 3/sqrt(c), project ball points to norm <=(1-1e-5)/sqrt(c), compute maps/distances in float32 with eps=1e-6, normalize only nonempty transition rows, use zero context for unsupported items, and clamp distance arguments to valid domains.
ideas.spec_equations: p_i(j)=count_train(i,j)^0.75/sum_{u in Top16(i)}count_train(i,u)^0.75; h_i=sum_j p_i(j)x_j; z_i=exp^c_0(W e_i); b_i=exp^c_0(U h_i); y_i=log^c_0(exp^c_{z_i}(alpha log^c_{z_i}(b_i))); k_i^l=argmin_k d_c(y_i-r_i^l,q_lk)^2. Use baseline STE and reconstruction/commitment losses; do not add a separate behavior-only objective.
ideas.spec_inputs_outputs: Inputs: frozen item embeddings, training-split sequences, encoder outputs, residual codebooks. Output: per-item residual code indices/SIDs and the unchanged reconstruction loss path.

specification.text: Let x_i be the frozen item embedding and e_i its encoder output. For each item i, compute p_i(j) proportional to count(i->j)^0.75 over outgoing training transitions, retaining top 16 successors; let h_i be their mean frozen embeddings. Map z_i=exp^c_0(W e_i) and b_i=exp^c_0(U h_i) into the ball of curvature -c (c=0.5). Define v_i=log^c_{z_i}(b_i), and transformed residual target y_i=log^c_0(exp^c_{z_i}(alpha v_i)), alpha=0.15. At quantizer level l choose k=argmin_k d_c(y_i-r_i^l, q_lk)^2, then r_i^(l+1)=r_i^l+q_lk in tangent coordinates; retain baseline straight-through update and reconstruction loss. Apply behavior through v_i only for items with at least two observed successors; otherwise set v_i=0.

ideas.title: User-branch tangent prototypes for residual code assignment

ideas.ablation_behavior_off: Set p_i uniform-independent by setting g_i=0 and disable transition-derived m_i; retain curved quantization and baseline target z_i.
ideas.ablation_both_on: Use training transition probabilities, entropy gate, curved Frechet mean, geodesic interpolation and Poincare assignment with curvature -0.5.
ideas.ablation_geometry_off: Retain training p_i and g_i but replace the Frechet/geodesic operations with weighted Euclidean neighbor mean and linear interpolation and squared Euclidean assignment.
ideas.behavior_computation: On training-only chronological user sequences, count each adjacent pair; form p_i over top 16 successors using add-one smoothing followed by renormalization; compute normalized entropy and weighted successor embedding mean.
ideas.behavior_signal: Per-item directed next-item neighborhood distribution and its normalized branching entropy.
ideas.cost_estimate: Precompute sparse neighbor lists and entropy once. Cache item z_j and m_i once per epoch (one batched 3-iteration neighborhood aggregation, O(24,556*16*d) map work); per training step add O(B*L*d) maps and no additional codebook scan beyond existing comparisons. Across 3,000 epochs/24 steps, cached neighbor update is 3,000*24,556*16*d scalar operations, while step overhead is about O(24*3,000*B*L*d), approximately 5-12% wall-clock if the codebook search dominates.
ideas.coupling_equation: m_i=FrechetMean_c({z_j,p_i(j)}); t_i=exp^c_{z_i}(beta*g_i*log^c_{z_i}(m_i)); k_i^1=argmin_k d_c(t_i,q_1k)^2, with p_i and g_i computed from training transitions.
ideas.coupling_path: The directed transition distribution defines the curved Frechet mean; its entropy gates a geodesic move from each encoded item toward that mean; the moved point is then directly quantized, changing code indices and gradients.
ideas.falsifiable_hypothesis: High-entropy transition neighborhoods are better represented by a curved local continuation barycenter than by a Euclidean reconstruction-only code; the effect should improve next-item prefix utility and Stage3 test Recall@10, with target above 0.065.
ideas.hyperbolic_location: A transition-neighborhood Frechet mean and entropy-gated geodesic target shift are computed inside the quantization forward path before the first residual assignment.
ideas.hyperbolic_operator: Poincare geodesic interpolation via log^c_z, exp^c_z and distance d_c, with fixed curvature -0.5.
ideas.key_change: Maintain a slowly updated Poincare prototype for each item’s observed next-item neighborhood and interpolate the item latent toward that prototype along the geodesic before residual quantization; the interpolation weight is the item’s empirical transition entropy, so highly branching items receive more continuation structure.
ideas.leakage_boundary: Training interactions alone produce graph, probabilities, entropy and neighbor lists; validation/test interactions are excluded from statistics, prototype initialization, training, and SID export.
ideas.motivation: Next-item prediction depends on local directed transitions, but ordinary codebook centroids are optimized to reconstruct item embeddings rather than to preserve the geometry of likely continuations.
ideas.novelty: Rather than attach graph regularization to an otherwise standard quantizer, this uses the training-only transition graph to construct geodesic barycentric targets that directly determine the RQ-VAE codebook assignment and its gradient.
ideas.observables: Assignment changes should concentrate among high-entropy items; test whether SID-prefix next-item ranking and Stage3 Recall@10 improve, and report assignment/gradient changes relative to baseline.
risks: Neighborhood barycenters can collapse unrelated branches; popularity bias may pull prototypes toward hubs; stale cached embeddings can make means inconsistent; small item support makes entropy unreliable.

ideas.spec_equations: p_i(j) from training counts; H_i=-sum_j p_i(j)log(p_i(j)+eps); g_i=H_i/log(max(2,degree_i)); m_i <- exp^c_{m_i}(eta sum_j p_i(j)log^c_{m_i}(z_j)) for 3 iterations; t_i=exp^c_{z_i}(beta*g_i*log^c_{z_i}(m_i)); quantize t_i by nearest geodesic code then quantize tangent residuals.
ideas.spec_inputs_outputs: Inputs: train-split sequences, frozen item embeddings, current encoder outputs and residual codebooks. Outputs: curved neighborhood targets, residual code assignments/SIDs, and gradients through the target path.

specification.text: From training sequences count outgoing pairs, compute normalized p_i(j), entropy H_i=-sum_j p_i(j)log(p_i(j)+eps), and gate g_i=clip(H_i/log(max(2,degree_i)),0,1) (set 0 for degree<2). Given encoded z_i=exp^c_0(W e_i), compute neighborhood prototype m_i as the 3-step weighted Frechet mean initialized at weighted Euclidean mean of exp^c_0(W x_j): m <- exp^c_m(eta*sum_j p_i(j)log^c_m(z_j)); eta=0.25. Use target t_i=exp^c_{z_i}(beta*g_i*log^c_{z_i}(m_i)), beta=0.2, then assign first residual code by argmin_k d_c(t_i,q_1k)^2; later levels quantize tangent residual log^c_0(t_i)-sum_{s<l}q_sk. Backpropagate through t_i and maps; update codebooks with baseline commitment/reconstruction losses.

findings.detail: artanh clamps to 1 - 1e-10. findings.correction: Implement the actual Poincare `exp_z(u) = z (+_c) exp0((lambda_z/2)u)` with a numerically safe Mobius addition and `u=alpha*log_z(b)`, then map the resulting ball point through `log0`; add an identity test comparing the basepoint distance from z to the prescribed tangent length and finite backward checks through this corrected path. findings.detail: `_log_at(z,b,c)` returns a tangent vector at z, but code forms `exp0(z + alpha*tangent)` and then `log0`. This treats the ball coordinate z as an origin-tangent vector and applies exp at the origin, rather than computing `exp_z(alpha * log_z(b))` as required. Consequently the behavior-conditioned curved displacement and resulting target/gradient are not the proposed geodesic transport. The checked-in smoke only compares `_log_at` to itself algebraically and checks that ablation gradients differ; it does not validate the exp-at-z identity, and therefore does not catch this error.
findings.reproduction: For any nonzero z and nonzero tangent v, compare the implementation's `_log0(_exp0(z + alpha*v,c),c)` against the Poincare expression `log0(mobius_add(z, exp0_at_origin((lambda_z * alpha * v))))`, where `lambda_z=2/(1-c*||z||^2)` and `mobius_add` is the ball Mobius addition. These are generally unequal; a direct test can additionally verify that `d_c(z, exp_z(alpha*v))` equals `alpha * ||v||_z` within tolerance. This is a code-level counterexample, not a runtime claim.
